text:
Donald Trump was seen watching himself on live TV ahead of his America 250 address(Image: X/@brenonade)

A photograph of President Donald Trump watching himself on Fox News shortly before his address at the America 250 event has been circulating online.

Trump was photographed at the National Mall alongside first lady Melania Trump before delivering remarks at the Salute to America event, which was organized as part of the country's 250th birthday celebration.

A video shows Fox News hosts asking the president to wave to the crowd as the president appears not to respond for a while. Eventually, he is seen waving at the crowd and watching himself wave live on TV.

“Hey, he's waving!” host Bret Baier said.

“Oh, the president waved?” asked Harris Faulkner, who was also on the panel.

“I think we just got a wave – I'm going to say it happened!” Baier said.

The America 250 celebrations in the past few days have been thrown into chaos as high temperatures deterred crowds from attending the Great American State Fair.

"By the way, on July 4, it’s going to be approximately 107 degrees out, and I’m going to go, and I’m going to make a really long speech just to show that I can do anything," the president said ahead of the address during his appearance at the opening ceremony for the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota. It came as Washington, D.C. was facing extreme temperatures, only beaten by those in the Gobi and Sahara Deserts.

Freedom 250, the Trump administration's organization operating the Great American State Fair along the National Mall, was also behind the Salute to America event. Trump previously touted the event as "the most spectacular TRUMP RALLY of them all."

During his address, Trump claimed that over 375,000 people came to watch him before the event was delayed. "They estimated they had 375,000 people before everybody had to leave, and they now have 150,000 people. It's the craziest thing anyone's ever seen," Trump said.

"There is no way we could be deterred," the president said, referring to his address.

So far, the 250th birthday celebrations in D.C. have seen many obstacles. The Great American State Fair, being held on the National Mall, was temporarily shut down because of the heat. Even a few days ago, much of the fanfare around the event floundered after many reports showed how empty the venue was.
